_doc: Which marker belongs to which gate, and whether passing by it is the gate's own rule path (a step done, a fact checked: rule_path true) or an override of the gate's judgement (rule_path false). Keyed by the label the refusal starts with (helpers/gate-label.cjs). ONE source for both readers: helpers/root-cause-gate.cjs (a refusal passed by an override marker holds until classified; a rule-path marker owes nothing) and scripts/gate-health.py (only an override gate is reported as 'errs often'). Operator 2026-11-23 (rule: a gate that errs is a finding); a mapping read from source text miscounted BETA-MERGE and PR-CLASS-OK (measured that day over 605 transcripts).
_way_on_doc: Phrases with which a refusal names its own way on - a pass after it is the gate followed, not a bypass. English built in here; other languages as instance data (way_on_patterns in .claude/rules/root-cause-patterns.json). Read by root-cause-gate.cjs and gate-health.py (Windows review of #640: most of 84 bypass signals were a gate's documented way on).

MECHANISM CHECK.why: 'Only if that path does not fit: # MECHANISM-OK: <why>' - an override of the documented path

CONDITIONAL-ORDER-GATE.why: '# CONDITION-NONE: ...' declares that the condition the gate read does not apply - its trigger was wrong

PR-OVERLAP.why: '# OVERLAP-OK: <why>' - the overlap the gate warns about is declared intended

PRS-FIRST.why: '# PRS-READ: <which one is closest>' records the reading the gate asks for

merge-request-gate.why: both record a checked fact: the system checked, where the request was answered

release-freeze-gate.why: '# SCOPE-OK: "<the operator's words>" <date>' quotes the operator

review-claim-gate.why: '# DIFF-READ: <where it was read>' records the reading

START-REPORT-GATE.why: '# START-REPORT-OK: <quoted order>' quotes the operator's order
